text:
Cutter Gauthier scored three more goals on Tuesday night and somehow it was not the story of the game. The Ducks winger finished with three goals and an assist on eight shots in St. Louis, and Daily Faceoff noted he became the first NHLer to record four hat tricks in one month. His goal streak, which headlines had at nine games after Sunday's win over Calgary, kept going too. The Blues still won 8-6, because for most of the night they were simply the better team.

St. Louis owned the first period, out-chancing Anaheim 2.02 to 0.96 in expected goals (the quality of the chances, not just the count). Jonatan Berggren tipped one in at 2:13, Alex Killorn answered, and Connor McMichael batted a puck home with 53 seconds left in the period. Gauthier tied it 62 seconds into the second with a slap shot that had a 4% chance of going in. Then Robert Thomas took over. His wrister at 11:41 of the second pushed the Blues' win chance from 52% to 73%, the biggest swing of the night, and Dalibor Dvorsky added another before Gauthier's power-play goal made it 4-3.

The third period was where Anaheim's goaltending gave out. Jake Neighbours, Philip Broberg (on a 2% deflection) and Logan Mailloux scored inside three minutes, and Ville Husso had allowed seven on 24 shots, three more than those shots deserved, before Lukas Dostal came on. Mailloux, who only made his season debut on Nov. 10 after coming off injured reserve, had a goal and two assists. Thomas had a goal and two helpers in under 17 minutes, and the Blues out-chanced Anaheim 1.90 to 0.36 in expected goals while he was on the ice.

Then the late chaos. Ian Moore, Mikael Granlund on the power play and Gauthier again pulled Anaheim to 7-6 with 41 seconds left, before Pavel Buchnevich scored three seconds later to end it. It flattered the Ducks: at even strength St. Louis generated 4.35 expected goals to 1.76, and the Blues deserved to win 69% of the time by our replays of every shot.

The uncomfortable footnote belongs to Jordan Binnington, whose name has been all over trade-rumour headlines for two weeks. He gave up six on 31 shots, 2.79 more than expected. A win is a win, but this was not the night that quiets that conversation.
headline: Gauthier's fourth hat trick of November isn't enough
